subject: maths

moments.title: Aryabhata
moments.body: At 23, Aryabhata writes the Aryabhatiya, including a remarkable approximation pi ≈ 3.1416, the sine function (jya), Earth's rotation explaining day-night, and the first table of sines.
moments.takeaway: Trigonometry is born in India in the 5th century.

moments.title: Brahmagupta and zero
moments.body: Brahmagupta gives arithmetic rules for zero and negative numbers. He also solves quadratic equations, including with negative solutions.
moments.takeaway: Zero becomes a number, not just a placeholder.

moments.title: Bhaskara II
moments.body: Bhaskara II's Lilavati and Siddhanta Shiromani anticipate calculus ideas, derivatives of sine, and Rolle's theorem. The Kerala school (14th-16th centuries) develops infinite series for trigonometric functions.
moments.takeaway: Calculus is foreshadowed in medieval India — 500 years before Newton.

moments.title: Al-Khwarizmi transmits
moments.body: al-Khwarizmi's books transmit Indian numerals and arithmetic to the Islamic world, and via translation to Europe. 'Algorithm' and 'algebra' come from his name and book title (al-jabr).
moments.takeaway: Indian numerals travel via Baghdad to Europe.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: The decimal place-value system is universal. Recent scholarship credits the Kerala school for proto-calculus more explicitly.
now.open_questions: How much modern mathematics ultimately traces to India, via Baghdad and beyond?

reflection: Calculus was foreshadowed in India 500 years before Newton-Leibniz. Why does the standard history start in 1660?
